newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels slaughter 13 villagers in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rebels slaughter 13 villagers in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed 13 villagers by cutting their throats in western Algerian, bringing to at least 120 the number of people killed in a four-day wave of massacres, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.

The guerrillas, suspected to be members of Algeria's ruthless Armed Islamic Group (GIA), stormed Merchiche hamlet in the western Tlemcen province, 440 km (225 miles) west of Algiers, at dusk on Sunday, said al Khabar newspaper.
The assailants killed some of 13 villagers by slashing their throats, took a dinner break and then slaughtered the others, including children and an elderly man, it said.
The rebels then left, aparently without encountering any resistance, the newspaper added.
The massacre was the latest in a series in which more than 120 people, mostly villagers in remote hamlets, have died between Thursday and last Sunday, according to Algerian newspapers.
In the worst attack in the five years of Algerian violence, Moslem guerrillas exterminated all the 52 inhabitants of Thalit village in Medea, 70 km (45 miles) southwest of Algiers, on Thursday.

The massacres coincided with huge operations by the army and security forces across the country in which more than 200 Moslem guerrillas have been killed since early in February, including several rebel leaders shot dead in their hideouts in Algiers.

They came after a short lull in the mass killings in which more than 300 died in massacres and bombings in Algiers and neighbouring towns after President Liamine Zeroual vowed on January 24 that his government would wipe out the guerrillas.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead. Algeria is to hold new parliamentary elections on June 5.
